title: Statistical Matching via Schrödinger Bridge beyond Conditional Independence
claim: Learn a joint coupling from separately observed datasets, impute missing variables in both directions, then merge the results to train a downstream predictor.
layout: 4 stages left-to-right, bracketed stage labels below, central Schrödinger bridge network diagram
description: A four-stage left-to-right pipeline, with a bracketed label under each stage. Stage 1, 'Observed marginals', shows a large box for the unobserved joint (X,Y,Z). Grayscale marginal histograms run along its left and bottom edges, and curved arrows lead from the observed pairs (X^A,Y^A) and (X^B,Z^B). Stage 2, 'Schrödinger bridge learning', is two stacked table-and-contour cards, one orange and one green, with missing columns left blank. Between them, two neural networks give potentials A(x,y) and B(x,z), joined by a red λ cost-tilting term under a blue glowing 'Schrödinger Bridge' title. Stage 3, 'Bidirectional imputation', has a joint density scatter with posterior formulas q*. Arrows lead to completed tables, with imputed columns in lighter shades. Stage 4 merges the datasets, trains a downstream network, and evaluates on held-out data. Orange, green and gray color-code the variables Y, Z and X.
caption: Overview of the proposed predictive statistical matching pipeline. The framework first learns the Schrödinger bridge potential functions to link the observed datasets DA and DB. It then performs bidirectional posterior completion to construct the imputed datasets ˆDA and ˆDB, which are subsequently merged to train and evaluate the downstream prediction model.
abstract: Statistical matching combines partially overlapping datasets that share covariates $X$ but observe the target $Y$ and auxiliary variables $Z$ separately. Classical approaches typically invoke the conditional independence assumption (CIA), which makes the problem identifiable but fundamentally implies that the imported auxiliary variable provides no additional predictive power for $Y$ once $X$ is known. To capture this latent $Y$--$Z$ dependence, we propose a novel dependency-aware SchrÃ¶dinger bridge for predictive statistical matching. Our approach couples the two separated databases by tilting the conservative CIA baseline with a transportation-based compatibility cost, recovering an informative joint distribution. The resulting statistical learning framework yields full probabilistic posterior rules for bidirectional imputation. Theoretically, we establish a sufficient condition under which the learned bridge strictly improves over the CIA baseline, alongside an exact joint recovery guarantee in the Gaussian setting under an appropriate cost. Across synthetic benchmarks and real-world datasets (CelebA and Adult), we demonstrate that our dependency-aware completion consistently improves downstream predictive utility, proving especially beneficial in settings like data recoding where the underlying population exhibits strong $Y$--$Z$ dependence.
